Effects by event time, cohort, period, or unit

Source: R/effects.R
trop_effects.Rd

trop_effects() averages the effects of the treated cells of a trop() fit in groups. A group is, for example, all treated cells with the same number of periods since the start of the treatment. The function can also give bootstrap standard errors, intervals, and simultaneous bands for all groups.

Usage

trop_effects(
  fit,
  by = c("event_time", "cohort", "time", "unit", "overall"),
  window = NULL,
  n_boot = NULL,
  boot_rows = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  resample = NULL,
  conf_level = fit$conf.level,
  ci = c("normal", "percentile"),
  seed = NULL,
  anticipation = 0L,
  weights = c("cell", "unit"),
  unit_weights = NULL,
  checkpoint = NULL,
  progress = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'trop_effects'
print(x, digits = 4L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'trop_effects'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'trop_effects'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'trop_effects'
vcov(object, ...)

Arguments

fit

A trop object from trop() or trop_matrix() with method = "local".

by

The groups. Refer to the section Groups.

window

An optional vector with 2 event times. The function uses cells with an event time from window[1] to window[2].

n_boot

The number of new bootstrap draws. With NULL, the function uses the draws of the fit, if the fit has draws. With 0, the function does not calculate a bootstrap.

boot_rows

A matrix of draws from trop_boot_rows(). This argument replaces n_boot.

strata, resample

The settings for new draws. Refer to trop_boot_rows(). With resample = NULL, the function uses the setting of the fit.

conf_level

The confidence level. The default is the level of the fit.

ci

Use "normal" or "percentile". Refer to trop().

seed

An optional integer seed for new draws. The function does not change the state of the random number generator in the R session.

anticipation

The number of treated periods at the start of each run that come before the true start. Refer to the section Anticipation. The default 0 uses the first treated period as the start.

weights

Use "cell" or "unit". Refer to the section Weights.

unit_weights

An optional numeric vector with one weight of 0 or more for each unit. A named vector must have a value for each unit name of the fit. A vector without names must be in the order of the rows of the panel.

checkpoint

An optional path of a file for the bootstrap draws. Refer to the section Long runs.

progress

Logical. If TRUE, the function shows the progress of the bootstrap.

x

A trop_effects object.

digits

The number of significant digits to show.

...

Not used.

row.names, optional

Not used.

object

A trop_effects object.

Value

A data frame of class trop_effects with one row for each group. The columns are the group (the name of the column is the value of by), estimate, n_cells, and n_units. With a bootstrap, the columns std.error, conf.low, conf.high, band.low, band.high, and n_draws are also in the data frame. The data frame has these attributes: draws (a matrix with one column for each group), rows (the rows of the draws), critical (the critical value of the band), n_complete (the number of draws with a value for all groups), diagnostics, and units (the names of the units of the fit). When by is a list, the result is a named list of such data frames.

coef() gives the estimates with the group names. vcov() gives the covariance matrix of the draws, from the draws with a value for all groups.

Details

The function uses the effects tau of the fit. Thus, the target cells of the fit are the only cells in the groups. A cell that has no effect in the fit, for example a cell outside of the target, is not in a group. A group with no such cell is not in the result. Use trop_cells() to count the cells of each group before you calculate the bootstrap.

Groups

The argument by sets the groups:

  • "event_time": the number of periods since the start of the current treatment. The value 0 is the first treated period. If a unit stops the treatment and starts it again, the count starts again.

  • "cohort": the period in which the current treatment started.

  • "time": the period.

  • "unit": the unit.

  • "overall": one group with all cells. The result is the ATT.

  • A matrix with the dimensions of the panel. The values are the group of each cell. A cell with NA is not in a group. Only treated cells with an effect are in groups.

  • A named list of the values above, for example list(event = "event_time", cohort = "cohort"). The function then gives a named list with one result for each element. All results use the same bootstrap draws, and the function calculates the estimator only one time for each draw. A character element without a name uses its value as the name.

The argument window limits the cells to cells with an event time in the window. For example, window = c(0, 3) uses the first 4 treated periods.

Anticipation

Sometimes the treatment has an effect before it starts, for example when units know the start date. A usual procedure is to set W = 1 in the periods before the start, so that these cells are not controls. Then, the first W = 1 cell is not the true start.

With anticipation = k, the function counts the first k treated periods of each run as the periods before the start. Thus, these periods get the event times -k to -1, and the event time 0 is the true start. The cohort is also the period of the true start. A cohort that starts after the last period of the panel is not in a group.

To keep the anticipation cells out of the estimate, also remove them from the target of the fit. Use trop_rollout() to make W and target from the start dates.

The function finds the start of each run from W. If a run starts in the first period of the panel, its anticipation periods can be before the panel. Then the event times of the run can be wrong, and the function gives a warning message. If the fit has event times from the argument event_time of trop(), the function uses them. Then anticipation must be 0. Refer to the section Event times of trop().

Weights

By default, each cell in a group has the same weight. Thus, a unit with more cells in a group has more weight in the group. With weights = "unit", each unit has the same total weight in each group. The function divides the weight of a unit by its number of cells in the group.

The weights are relative. In each group, the function divides the weights by the largest weight of the units of that group. Thus, the estimate of a group does not depend on the weights of other units. In a group, the largest positive weight must be less than 1e200 times the smallest positive weight.

With unit_weights, each unit has its own weight, for example its number of workers before the treatment. Use weights that the treatment cannot change. With weights = "cell", each cell gets the weight of its unit. With weights = "unit", the weight of a unit is its total weight in each group. A unit with a weight of 0 is not in a group.

The bootstrap uses the same weights. A unit that a draw selects two times counts as two units in the draw. The ATT of the fit always gives the same weight to each cell.

Inference

The bootstrap uses the unit draws of the fit. For each draw, the function calculates the local estimator again with the tuning parameters of the fit. Then it averages the effects of each group. The tuning parameters do not change. The standard error of a group is the standard deviation of its draws.

A group that has no treated cell in a draw has no value for that draw. The column n_draws gives the number of draws with a value for each group.

The draws run in parallel with the threads of the control of the fit.

By default, the function uses the draws that the fit stored in fit$boot$rows. Then the average of all treated cells has the same draws as fit$boot$draws. With n_boot, the function makes new draws. With boot_rows, you give the draws. A group of one fit and a group of another fit have a joint distribution only if they use the same draws.

Each call calculates the estimator again for each draw. To get many sets of groups, give them in one list to by. To calculate the draws only one time, make the fit with se = "none". Then include "overall" in the list, and give the draws with boot_rows.

The columns band.low and band.high give a simultaneous band with the sup-t method. The band has a critical value for all groups. The critical value is a quantile of the largest absolute value of the standardized draws over the groups. The band contains all true group effects with the probability conf_level, if the bootstrap is correct.

The band uses only the draws with a value for all groups. The centers and the standard errors of the band also come from these draws. Thus, if some draws have no value for a group, the band and the interval of that group use different draws. If fewer than 2 draws have a value for all groups, the band is not available.

The intervals conf.low and conf.high are for one group each. The band needs many draws. With only one group, the band columns are NA.

Diagnostics

The attribute diagnostics is a data frame with one row for each draw. Its columns count these cells and fits of the draw:

  • n_used: the treated cells with an effect.

  • n_skipped: the cells that the untreated cells do not identify.

  • n_nonconverged: the fits that did not converge.

  • n_failed: the fits that failed. A fit fails if the singular value decomposition fails or if the result is not finite.

  • n_dropped: the cells that have an effect in the fit, but that the untreated cells of the draw do not identify. The count does not include the fits that failed.

The function gives a warning message when a draw has such fits or cells. It also gives a warning message for a group with fewer than 2 draws with a value. The print method shows these counts.

Long runs

With progress = TRUE, the function shows the number of draws that are done and an estimate of the time that is left. With checkpoint, the function saves the draws to a file after each block of draws. If the calculation stops, call the function again with the same arguments and the same file. The function then calculates only the draws that are not in the file. The results are equal to the results of one run without a stop.

The file has a fingerprint of the calculation. The fingerprint uses the panel, the tuning parameters, the solver settings, the draw rows, the groups, the weights, and the version of fasttrop. If the fingerprint of the file is different, the function stops with an error and does not change the file. The number of threads is not in the fingerprint, because it does not change the results.

The file is an RDS file with the draws, but not the panel. Keep it in a folder on your computer. The function makes sure that it can write to the folder before it starts the bootstrap.

See also

trop_cells(), trop_contrast(), trop_boot_rows(), trop_stepdown()

Examples

sim <- trop_simulate(n_units = 20, n_periods = 12, n_treated = 5,
                     n_post = 3, effect = 1, seed = 1)
fit <- trop(sim, "y", "d", "unit", "time",
            lambda = c(time = 0.2, unit = 0.5, nn = 0.5),
            n_boot = 50, seed = 1, control = trop_control(threads = 1))
trop_effects(fit, by = "event_time")
#> TROP effects by event time
#>   Weights: each cell has the same weight.
#>  event_time estimate n_cells n_units std.error conf.low conf.high band.low
#>           0  1.41712       5       5    0.3535   0.7243     2.110   0.6428
#>           1  1.97684       5       5    0.4643   1.0669     2.887   0.9599
#>           2 -0.03763       5       5    0.3825  -0.7873     0.712  -0.8755
#>  band.high n_draws
#>     2.1914      50
#>     2.9938      50
#>     0.8002      50
#> Bootstrap: 50 draws. The band is simultaneous (sup-t) at the 95% level. It uses the 50 draws with a value for all rows.

# Two sets of groups with one bootstrap sweep.
both <- trop_effects(fit, by = list(event = "event_time", time = "time"))
trop_stepdown(both)
#> Romano-Wolf stepdown p-values
#>      name estimate std.error        t   p_raw   p_adj
#>  event: 0  1.41712    0.3535  4.00906 0.01961 0.01961
#>  event: 1  1.97684    0.4643  4.25805 0.01961 0.01961
#>  event: 2 -0.03763    0.3825 -0.09838 0.90196 0.90196
#>  time: 10  1.41712    0.3535  4.00906 0.01961 0.01961
#>  time: 11  1.97684    0.4643  4.25805 0.01961 0.01961
#>  time: 12 -0.03763    0.3825 -0.09838 0.90196 0.90196
#> Draws: 50 of 50 have a value for all estimates. The p-values use these draws.
